The paper presents a capillary-wave description of binary-alloy solidification, generalizing a previously introduced model to include the procedure of directional solidification.
A universal dispersion relation of the unstable eigenmodes of a planar steady-state solidification front is derived, which readjusts previously known stability considerations.
The paper establishes a differential equation for oscillatory motions of a planar interface that offers a limit-cycle scenario for the formation of solute bands and banded structures.
The model considers the simplest case of a planar interface, neglecting heat diffusion and assuming an overall constant diffusion coefficient for the solute component.
For a class of model systems, the resulting integro-differential equation for the interface position can be reduced to the differential equation of a damped nonlinear oscillator.
Stationary solutions of the oscillator equation are found to exist in some region, limited by the threshold of the Cahn instability.
The nature of the periodic solutions can be tuned from almost-harmonic to distinctive relaxation oscillations by changing the pulling velocity.
The inclusion of the inertial term in the oscillator equation is crucial for providing the necessary turnaround of the trajectories at low velocities.
The projection of the limit cycle enters the unstable region of the Mullins-Sekerka instability, leading to the development of a dendritic microstructure at low velocities.
The period of the limit cycle is proportional to m near the threshold, and proportional to m² deep inside the limit-cycle regime, where m is a parameter related to the temperature gradient.
The reduced model equations emerge in the limit of an infinite heat conductivity from a more general model involving energy density as an additional field variable.
The paper demonstrates that the periodic motion of a planar solidification front can only be explained by going one step beyond the quasi-stationary approximation.
The Cahn instability, similar to that found in grain-boundary motion, acts as a seed for the limit-cycle behavior in the unstable regime.

The inertial term in the oscillator equation proves to be important for the formation of a hysteresis loop, which represents the limit cycle describing the defect oscillations necessary for the creation of banded structures.
The model choice of the solute concentration profile U(z-Z) leads to explicit expressions for the quantities G(v) and C(Z(t),t), which are used in the analysis.
